questions.text: Which of the following is a part of adenohypophysis?
questions.explanation: The adenohypophysis consists of pars distalis, pars tuberalis, and pars intermedia.

questions.text: The pituitary gland lies in the ___ of the sphenoid bone and is connected to the hypothalamus by the ___.
questions.explanation: The hypophysis occupies the sella turcica and communicates with the hypothalamus through the infundibulum.

questions.text: Describe the regulation of growth hormone secretion.
questions.modelAnswer: Growth hormone secretion is stimulated mainly by growth hormone-releasing hormone and ghrelin, and inhibited by somatostatin. Secretion is pulsatile, increases during deep sleep, exercise, fasting, hypoglycemia, stress, and puberty, and decreases with hyperglycemia, elevated free fatty acids, aging, and negative feedback from insulin-like growth factor 1.
questions.explanation: Growth hormone is controlled by hypothalamic releasing and inhibiting hormones, metabolic cues, sleep, stress, and IGF-1 negative feedback.
questions.keyConcept: Pulsatile GH secretion and hypothalamic control

questions.text: Prolactin secretion is predominantly inhibited by hypothalamic dopamine.
questions.explanation: Dopamine exerts tonic inhibition on lactotrophs, so interruption of hypothalamic dopamine delivery increases prolactin secretion.

chapters.title: Thyroid and Parathyroid Glands
chapters.subtitle: Hormone synthesis, calcium homeostasis, and clinical disorders

questions.text: Match each thyroid hormone synthesis step with its description.

pairs.target: Active transport of iodide into follicular cells through the sodium-iodide symporter
Oxidation and attachment of iodine to tyrosyl residues on thyroglobulin
Combination of iodotyrosines to form T3 and T4

questions.explanation: Thyroid hormone synthesis proceeds through iodide uptake, oxidation and organification, coupling, storage, and proteolytic release.
questions.keyConcept: Sequential biochemical steps of thyroid hormone synthesis

questions.text: A 28-year-old woman presents with weight loss, heat intolerance, tremor, palpitations, and diffuse thyroid enlargement. Laboratory tests show suppressed TSH and elevated free T4.
questions.explanation: The presentation is most consistent with Graves disease causing primary hyperthyroidism.
questions.keyConcept: Clinical and biochemical diagnosis of hyperthyroidism

subQuestions.explanation: Diffuse goiter with thyrotoxic symptoms and suppressed TSH with elevated free T4 is typical of Graves disease.
subQuestions.keyConcept: Graves disease is a common cause of primary hyperthyroidism

subQuestions.text: Explain the expected thyroid function test pattern in primary hyperthyroidism.
subQuestions.modelAnswer: Primary hyperthyroidism causes excessive thyroid hormone production by the thyroid gland. Free T4 and/or T3 are elevated, and pituitary TSH is suppressed by negative feedback.
subQuestions.explanation: High circulating thyroid hormone suppresses TSH secretion through negative feedback at the pituitary and hypothalamus.
subQuestions.keyConcept: Low TSH with high free T4 indicates primary hyperthyroidism

questions.text: Which laboratory pattern is most consistent with primary hypoparathyroidism?
options: High calcium, high phosphate, high parathyroid hormone
Low calcium, high phosphate, low parathyroid hormone
Low calcium, low phosphate, high parathyroid hormone
High calcium, low phosphate, low parathyroid hormone
questions.explanation: Primary hypoparathyroidism causes deficient parathyroid hormone secretion, producing hypocalcemia and hyperphosphatemia.
questions.keyConcept: PTH raises serum calcium and lowers serum phosphate
